outcome: No resolution, partial case settlement, or bound movement was found since 26 January 2024; the core question of whether every integer not congruent to 4 or 5 (mod 9) is a sum of three cubes remains open, and the seven small cases below 1000 (114, 390, 627, 633, 732, 921, 975) remain unsolved.
summary: I searched for any development on the sum-of-three-cubes characterization question since 26 January 2024 and found nothing that changes the problem's status. The one item the triage flagged, arXiv:2512.15763 ('Representation Of Integers By Sum Of Three Cubes, A New Approach Based On Seed Equation'), was submitted to arXiv on 12 December 2025, but its own journal-reference field states it was originally published in Mathematical Forum, Vol. 28(2), 2020 — i.e. this is an old (pre-2024) paper newly deposited on arXiv, not new work, and it does not address the mod-9 sufficiency question or any of the outstanding small cases (114, 390, 627, 633, 732, 921, 975); its abstract makes no mention of them. The last genuine mathematical events on this problem (Booker's 2019 resolution of 33, and Booker–Sutherland's 2019 resolution of 42 and third representation of 3) predate the window entirely and are already reflected in Wikipedia's current article, which still states plainly that whether the mod-9 necessary condition is sufficient 'is unknown.' A 2024 paper on 'Diophantine imaging' (Sultanow, Henkel, Aberkane, Scientific Reports, published 2 January 2024, DOI 10.1038/s41598-023-49960-y) offers a visualization method for known solution datasets; it was published four days before the frozen revision's 26 January 2024 timestamp, so even setting scope aside it falls outside the window, and in any case it is a descriptive/visualization tool, not a case settled or a bound moved, and involves no AI system. I also checked Epoch AI's FrontierMath 'Open Problems' page, which lists sum of three cubes as an open benchmark challenge for AI systems (specifically, finding a fourth representation for n=3) but reports no successful AI attempt — it frames the problem as unsolved by AI, not solved. Searches for AI-specific efforts (AlphaProof, AlphaGeometry, LLM-based approaches) turned up no application to this problem; those systems' publicized results are in geometry and olympiad problem-solving, not this Diophantine search problem. No credible source reports any of the seven remaining sub-1000 cases being resolved, any new admissible/inadmissible residue class established, or any AI system producing a representation. The status is therefore open with no_change_found true.
competing_reading: One could argue the December 2025 arXiv posting of 2512.15763 constitutes a dated 'event' worth recording as `progress`, since it is new to arXiv even if the underlying work is from 2020. I judged this incorrect: the mathematical content demonstrably predates the frozen revision (it's a 2020 publication), so treating its arXiv upload date as the event date would misattribute a stale paper as new progress, which is exactly the failure mode the open_stale category exists to prevent — except here the paper doesn't even settle a case or move a bound, so it isn't `open_stale` either, just irrelevant.
what_would_settle_it: A dated preprint or publication that either (a) proves or disproves the mod-9 sufficiency conjecture in general, (b) finds a representation for one of 114, 390, 627, 633, 732, 921, or 975 (or proves one impossible), or (c) an AI-lab report (e.g. from Epoch AI's FrontierMath benchmark, DeepMind, or similar) describing a model finding a new representation such as a fourth solution for n=3.
